title: Logout reports success even when server-side sign-out fails
reasoning: logout awaits fetch but never checks response.ok or parses an error. Any HTTP 401/403/500 response resolves as a successful Promise<void>, so callers can clear local auth state while the server-side cookie/session may remain valid because the request used credentials: 'include'. The linked test only mocks logout and verifies it was called plus localStorage was cleared, so it encodes the current blind spot rather than protecting server sign-out semantics.
reproduction: Have /users/sign_out return HTTP 500 or 401. await logout(token) still resolves, allowing the UI flow to proceed as if sign-out succeeded.
recommendation: Mirror login's failure handling: check response.ok, tolerate empty/non-JSON error bodies, and throw a meaningful error when sign-out is rejected so the auth flow can decide whether to retry, warn, or avoid claiming server logout succeeded.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The integration test mocks '@/api/auth' entirely, so the real fetch response handling in logout is never exercised. It also asserts only that logout was called, not that failed sign-out responses reject.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for logout with fetch mocked to return ok: false and assert that logout rejects with a useful error and does not silently resolve.
minimumFixScope: Update app/api/auth.ts logout response handling and add focused tests for successful and failed logout fetch responses.
